nodes.name: Pt₁/CeO₂ thermal shock synthesis
nodes.procedure: Datye et al. have modified the local environment of isolated Pt²⁺ by thermal-shock (TS) synthesis to obtain a highly active and thermally stable Pt₁/CeO₂ catalyst. TS synthesis stabilizes the asymmetric Pt₁O₄ configuration isolated Pt²⁺ by inducing a strong surface reconstruction of CeO₂ in an inert atmosphere, while limiting the gas-phase migration of PtO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: ZIF-NC-0.5Fe-700 shows increased pre-edge intensity after thermal activation at 700°C, indicating lower symmetry around Fe atoms or shorter Fe-N bond lengths in Fe-N4 configuration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: for oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), after thermal activation at 700°C , the ZIF-NC-0.5Fe-700 has showed increased pre-edge intensity (Figure 3a), an indication of lower symmetry around the Fe atoms or shorter Fe-N bond lengths in the Fe - N4 configuration.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows pre-edge at approximately 8340 eV for all samples indicating partial oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pre-edge of X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) at approximately 8340 eV for all samples indicates a partial oxidation state resulting from free electron sharing between Ni and C, N, or O (Figure 3g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-N-C catalysts at 400°C and 900°C show Ni-N bond lengths of 1.85 Å and 1.62 Å respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni - N bond lengths of Ni - N - C catalysts at 400 and 900°C are 1.85 and 1.62Å respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt1-Fe2O3-ox shows Pt-O peak at about 1.6 Å, shorter than Pt1-Fe2O3; Pt-Fe contribution shows weak peak at 2.7 Å in Pt1-Fe2O3-ox.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Fourier transformed-extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) curves, Pt1-Fe2O3-ox has a Pt-O peak at about 1.6Å , which is shorter than Pt1-Fe2O3 (Figure 4e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-SAS/SNC main peak at 1.59 Å (Ru-N), average Ru-N bond length 1.886 Å; Ru-SAS/NC Ru-N peak at 1.50 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 5b, the main peak determined in Ru-SAS/SNC is located at 1.59 Å, which is slightly larger than the Ru-N peak/888 (1.50 Å) in Ru-SAS/NC and shorter than the appearance peak of Ru-S bond (1.81 Å).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-ISA/SNC shows two pairs of Fe-N bonds at 1.86 Å and 1.97 Å; Fe-ISA/NC shows single Fe-N bond length of 1.91 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fitted curves show that the Fe atoms in Fe-ISA/SNC are coordinated by four N atoms, but four Fe-N bonds split into two pairs, one pair of bonds being 1.86Å long and the other pair being 1.97Å long (Figure 5k).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu-SA/SNC shows Cu-N bond lengths of 1.95 Å; Cu-SA/NC shows longer Cu-N bond lengths of 2.00 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the first coordination shell, Cu atom is coordinated with four N atoms, and the bond lengths are 1.95Å . However, the Cu species in Cu-SA/NC exist as Cu - N4 - C10 , and the bond lengths of Cu - N are longer (2.00Å).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-FN-C shows Fe-N bond slightly expanded compared to Fe-N-C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results of EXAFS fitting and wavelet transform analysis showed that the Fe-N bond of Fe-FN-C expanded slightly compared with that of Fe-N-C, indicating that the bond length and electron distribution in Fe - N4 changed slightly (Figure 6e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni2NC shows pre-edge between Ni foil and NiO during CO2RR, with slight decrease in Ni oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As can be seen from the XANES spectrum (Figure 6g), the pre-edge of the Ni2NC sample during CO2RR is still located between that of the Ni foil and NiO, excluding the formation of metal Ni.
